name: Lumencia Academy
description: A prestigious imperial academy where martial cultivation, spellcraft and divine power meet, and noble privilege collides with commoner ambition.

summary.en: You arrive as a new student at Lumencia Academy, the most prestigious school of the empire, where sword arts, spellcraft and divine power are taught side by side. Classes, exams, rivalries and friendships between proud nobles and ambitious commoners... while a demonic cult stirs in the shadows.
summary.fr: Vous arrivez comme nouvel élève à l'Académie Lumencia, l'école la plus prestigieuse de l'empire, où l'on enseigne côte à côte l'art de l'épée, la magie et le pouvoir divin. Cours, examens, rivalités et amitiés entre nobles fiers et roturiers ambitieux… pendant qu'un culte démoniaque s'agite dans l'ombre.

purpose.en: You arrive at Lumencia Academy as a new student, on the first day of the academy year, for the entrance ceremony.
purpose.fr: Vous arrivez à l'Académie Lumencia comme nouvel élève, le premier jour de l'année académique, pour la cérémonie d'entrée.

starters.blueprint:
OPENING - ENROLLMENT. First day of the academy year (1 March) at Lumencia Academy in Asterion. The protagonist is a newly arrived first-year student attending the entrance ceremony in the grand hall. The entrance ceremony (Headmaster Emily's speech and the presentation of the three instructors) is fully played in the prologue below: never replay it or repeat its speeches. In the turns that follow, the protagonist chooses the wing they wish to join (Knight, Magic or Theology); a student who does not know yet may take the orientation exam run by the academy staff or the student council. First-year students arrived today, like the protagonist, and hold no official role. Never choose the wing for the protagonist and never decide their dialogue, feelings or actions.
YOUR REPLY FOR THIS OPENING: write the author's prologue below as the scene, almost word for word. Keep every line of dialogue and every portrait tag exactly as written and in the same order, keep the tone, add nothing after Emily's last line, and do not copy these instructions. The author's prologue:

The chill of dawn had not yet fully lifted from Asterion's air, and the road to the grand hall was gradually coming alive.
Dozens of carriages lined up before the main gate, while noble heirs in ornate ceremonial dress and commoner students in modest uniforms mingled as they walked toward the entrance.
The Lumencia Empire's crest, carved between marble pillars, gleamed gold in the morning light, and the plaza slowly filled with murmurs.
The bell to signal the opening ceremony had not yet tolled. But the waiting air carried a peculiar mix of tension and excitement.
Knight Department banners fluttered in the breeze, and the hems of Magic Department robes rippled gently. Professors and upperclassmen filed into the grand hall one by one, and a quiet shadow of discipline settled over the scene.
Soon the first bell would ring. And from that moment, another year at Lumencia Academy would begin.

The bell rang at last: one deep, clear note that rolled across the plaza and silenced it.

Inside, the grand hall swallowed the new students whole. Tall windows poured pale light over row upon row of benches. Nobles drifted toward the front out of habit, and commoners settled wherever they could. On the stage, the professors stood in a quiet line. Before them, behind a lectern far too large for her, stood a small silver-haired woman holding a cream puff.

She took a bite. Then another. Only when the last crumb was gone did she lean toward the lectern.

[Emily:2] "Good morning, everyone. Welcome to Lumencia Academy. I'm Emily, your Headmaster."

Confused whispers rippled through the benches. Unbothered, she licked a spot of cream from her thumb.

[Emily:2] "Let's start with the most important rule, so no one can say they didn't hear it."

Her smile stayed in place, but her blue eyes cooled.

[Emily:1] "Within these walls, there are no nobles and no commoners. Your father's title, your family's coin, the crest on your carriage... none of it exists here. There is only one status at Lumencia: student. And a student is worth exactly what their talent and their grades say. Nothing more. Nothing less."

Near the front, someone shifted uncomfortably. Emily reached for a second pastry from a small plate beside the lectern.

[Emily:1] "Second thing. Field trips, missions, exams... some of what you'll face here is dangerous. Some of it has been fatal."

She took a bite, chewed, swallowed.

[Emily:1] "So please be careful. I'd hate to learn your names only for a memorial."

Silence. Even the front rows had stopped whispering.

[Emily:2] "Well! Enough gloom from me. Let me introduce the people who will decide where you belong."

She stepped aside. A tall woman with white hair and red eyes came forward, her armour plain and her posture straight as a drawn blade.

[Artemis:1] "Artemis. Head Professor of the Knight Department. The Knight wing trains the body, the sword and the will. You will bleed, you will fall, and you will stand back up. Those who wish to join will face me in a duel. Do not expect me to go easy on you."

She stepped back without another word. The next woman strolled forward instead, blue hair loose over her robes, gold eyes amused.

[Elena Caldwin:2] "Elena Caldwin, Head Professor of the Magic Department. Don't let Artemis scare you. Magic is far more civilised: mana, circles, theory... and the occasional explosion. Candidates will stand before a mana detection crystal. It doesn't lie, so neither should you."

Last came a young woman in white, with calm pink eyes and the symbol of the Holy Kingdom of Dominus at her throat. Some in the hall recognised her at once: the Saintess, still a student herself.

[Aria:1] "I am Aria, and I will guide those who choose the Theology wing. Here you will learn faith, healing, and the strength that comes from serving others. Your trial will be one of the heart. I pray each of you finds where you belong."

Emily returned to the lectern, brushing crumbs from her sleeve.

[Emily:2] "Knight, Magic or Theology: choose the wing you wish to join. And if you truly don't know yet, the student council will hold an orientation exam after the ceremony."

Her gaze swept the hall and, for a moment, seemed to rest on each of them.

[Emily:2] "Choose well. Your year begins now."

events.brief: The entrance ceremony for the new students, on their first day, in the academy's great hall. Headmaster Emily welcomes them, presents the academy and its rules (conduct, ranks, the three wings: Knight, Magic and Theology), then introduces the three instructors who will evaluate the newcomers: Artemis for the Knight wing, Elena Caldwin for the Magic wing and Aria, the Saintess, for the Theology wing. It ends with the students having to choose the wing they will try to join.

Only for students who still do not know which wing to join: an orientation exam run by the academy staff or members of the student council, a series of short tests of body, mana and faith. The results point to the wing that would suit the protagonist best, but the choice stays the player's: end the scene on that choice.
The entrance evaluation of the wing the protagonist chose, run by its instructor in front of the other candidates. Its result sets the protagonist's starting rank in the wing.

variants.knight: Artemis evaluates each candidate in a one-on-one duel against her. She is far stronger and does not try to win quickly: she watches technique, reflexes, stamina and spirit, and pushes the candidate to their limit.
variants.magic: Elena Caldwin has each candidate stand before a mana detection crystal: its light (strength, colour, steadiness) reveals the amount and nature of their mana. She may ask for a simple spell afterwards; the other candidates watch and react to the results.
variants.divine: Aria, the Saintess, evaluates the Theology candidates. Invent the form of the test: a trial of faith and divine affinity fitting the traditions of the Holy Kingdom of Dominus (for example a prayer at an altar, a purification, healing a wound or a vision). Make it memorable.

title.fr: Événement de début d'année de l'aile

events.brief: A start-of-year event of the protagonist's wing, in which the protagonist takes part. It may be announced first and take place a few days later.

variants.knight: The Knight wing's start-of-year tournament: first-year duels in brackets, watched by students, instructors and some noble guests; a chance to climb in rank and to make rivals.
variants.magic: The Magic wing's start-of-year assignment: each first-year must invent an original spell, or write a short research thesis on a magical question, and present it before Elena Caldwin and the other students.
variants.divine: Invent the Theology wing's start-of-year event in the spirit of the wing (for example a pilgrimage, a purification mission in Asterion, a ceremony where the first-years receive a blessing, or help at a hospice), with Aria involved.

events.brief: The end-of-year final evaluation of the protagonist's wing, which sets the year-end ranking. Choose its form from what happened during the year: the protagonist's progress, strengths and weaknesses, rivals and unresolved conflicts.
